provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Twinkle twinkle new verses
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to state new words for the star rhyme.
The pupils should be able to perform actions in pairs.

Introduction:
We know the twinkle twinkle little star song.
Today we will add new star words.

Content:
We sing the first verse as usual.
Then we add new words like shiny bright star.
We make twinkling actions with our fingers.
Work in pairs to show twinkling to each other.

Class activity:
Pair up and take turns being the star.
The partner says the new star words.

Evaluation questions:
What new words did we add?
Show me twinkling action.
Who can say the new verse?

Summary:
We made our own star song with new words.

topics.title: Five little firemen
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count down from five.
The pupils should be able to demonstrate water spraying action.

Introduction:
We have learned counting songs before.
Today we sing about brave firemen.

Content:
We start with five little firemen standing tall.
Each verse one goes away until none are left.
We spray water like fire fighters do.
We bend low and aim our water spray.

Class activity:
Line up as five firemen.
Count down and spray water actions.

Evaluation questions:
Count the firemen down.
Show how fire fighters spray water.
Why do fire fighters help people?

Summary:
We learned to count down and help others.

topics.title: Ten fat sausages
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count down by twos.
The pupils should be able to perform pop and bang actions.

Introduction:
We can count down from ten by ones.
Today we count down by twos with sausages.

Content:
Ten fat sausages sizzling in the pan.
One goes pop and the other goes bang.
Eight fat sausages left in the pan.
We show pop with a jump and bang with a clap.

Class activity:
Stand in a circle holding pretend sausages.
Count down by twos and do pop and bang.

Evaluation questions:
How many sausages after first pop?
Show me the pop action.
Show me the bang action.

Summary:
We counted down by twos with fun actions.

topics.title: Miss Polly had a dolly
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to act as doctor and dolly.
The pupils should be able to explain caring for the sick.

Introduction:
We know dolls need care when they are sick.
Today we sing about Miss Polly and her dolly.

Content:
Miss Polly had a dolly who was sick sick sick.
So she called for the doctor quick quick quick.
The doctor came with his bag and hat.
He gave the dolly some medicine and she was well.

Class activity:
One pupil is Miss Polly with a doll.
Another pupil is the doctor with a bag.
Act out the song with gentle movements.

Evaluation questions:
What did Miss Polly do when dolly was sick?
Show how the doctor helps.
How do we care for sick friends?

Summary:
We learned to care for others when they are sick.

topics.title: Little Boy Blue
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the rhyme with actions.
The pupils should be able to name farm animals.

Introduction:
Some people work with animals on farms.
Today we sing about a boy who watches sheep.

Content:
Little Boy Blue come blow your horn.
The sheep's in the meadow the cow's in the corn.
Where is the boy who looks after the sheep?
He's fast asleep under the haystack.

Class activity:
Act out the rhyme with horn blowing.
Show sleeping under haystack.
Name other farm animals.

Evaluation questions:
What animals are in the rhyme?
Show how to blow a horn.
Where was Little Boy Blue sleeping?

Summary:
We learned about farm animals and their work.

topics.title: Polly put the kettle on
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recite the tea party rhyme.
The pupils should be able to show family roles.

Introduction:\ Families make tea together at home.
Today we sing about making tea with family.

Content:
Polly put the kettle on Polly put the kettle on.
We'll all have tea when the kettle's on.
Polly takes it off again Polly takes it off again.
We'll all have tea when the kettle's off.

Class activity:
Sit in a circle pretending to make tea.
Pass cups around and say the rhyme.

Evaluation questions:
What does Polly put on the stove?
Show how to take off the kettle.
Who drinks tea in your family?

Summary:
We learned about making tea with family.

topics.title: Wind the bobbin up
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to wind bobbin actions.
The pupils should be able to follow the song movements.

Introduction:
We can wind things with our hands.
Today we sing about winding and unwinding.

Content:
Wind the bobbin up wind the bobbin up.
Pull pull clap clap wind the bobbin up.
Point to the ceiling point to the floor.
Point to the window and point to the door.

Class activity:
Stand and do all the actions.
Wind arms up and down.
Point to different parts of the room.

Evaluation questions:
Show how to wind the bobbin.
What do we point to in the room?
How do we pull and clap?

Summary:
We followed the song with our bodies.

topics.title: One finger, one thumb
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add body parts to the song.
The pupils should be able to keep the beat.

Introduction:
We can count with our fingers and toes.
Today we add parts to our counting song.

Content:
One finger one thumb keep moving.
One finger one thumb keep moving.
Add one arm and keep moving.
Add one leg and keep moving.
Add your head and keep moving.

Class activity:
Start with fingers and add parts each time.
Keep moving all the time while singing.

Evaluation questions:
What body parts did we add?
Show how to keep moving.
Can you count with your body parts?

Summary:
We added body parts and kept moving.

topics.title: Clap your hands
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to clap in rhythm.
The pupils should be able to sing fast and slow.

Introduction:
We can make sounds with our hands.
Today we clap in different speeds.

Content:
Clap your hands clap your hands.
Clap your hands and turn around.
Clap your hands clap your hands.
Clap your hands and sit down.
We clap fast then we clap slow.

Class activity:
Form a circle and clap in time.
Change from fast to slow clapping.

Evaluation questions:
Show fast clapping.
Show slow clapping.
What do we do after clapping?

Summary:
We clapped in different speeds.

topics.title: Rhyme festival
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to perform term rhymes.
The pupils should be able to clap along with others.

Introduction:
We learned many rhymes this term.
Today we show our parents what we know.

Content:
We stand on stage and sing our favorite rhymes.
We do the actions we learned this term.
Parents clap and watch our performance.
We smile and sing loudly for everyone.

Class activity:
Practice all rhymes for the festival.
Take turns performing on the stage.

Evaluation questions:
Which rhyme is your favorite?
Show your best action.
How do we thank the audience?

Summary:
We performed all our rhymes for parents.
